subject: Urgent: Orbit Commerce checkout 504 spike — suspected KV-cache / batching amplification
messages:
From: Thalia Ramos <thalia@orbitcommerce.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: checkout service 504s starting 08:45 PT — urgent

Stephanie —

We’re seeing a severe spike in 504s on our checkout integration that started ~08:45 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.6% to ~18% and p95 latency climbed from 520ms to 3.4s. Our clients are receiving timeouts and the SDK is aggressively retrying which looks like a retry-storm and making the problem worse.

We captured traces and a perf dump (attached). We have launch traffic scheduled for 11:00 PT and this is already impacting purchases. Can you put us on an incident bridge and advise immediate mitigations?

Request ids we see in the logs: 2a7f3b1c, 2a7f3b1d, 2a7f3b2a (attached csv).

Thalia

thalia@orbitcommerce.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20 09:33 AM PDT
Subject: Orbit Commerce — triage notes (logs + hypothesis)

Markus / Sean —
We’ve pulled the traces Thalia attached and live metrics on the route orbit-checkout.v1. Observations:
- Rapid jump in 5xx/429 starting 08:45 PT, sustained for ~35m.
- p95 tokenized latency 3.2–3.6s; backend GPU CPU utilization spiked on a small subset of hosts.
- We see many requests falling back from KV lookup to full compute; each fallback triggers large batches which then queue behind long-running requests.
- Client retries are exponential and overlapping which looks like a retry amplification / batching coupling effect.

Hypothesis: a regression in KV-cache lookup path under concurrent prefix eviction. When a cache miss occurs, the request goes to full model inference and gets batched; if multiple misses happen simultaneously the batch coalescer amasses a large batch and overloads the worker causing queueing and 504s.

Short-term mitigation proposals (low-risk):
1) Reduce batch coalescing window for orbit-checkout.v1 from 50ms -> 10ms (reduces amplification).
2) Temporarily disable prefix cache for orbit-checkout route (avoid repeated fallback storms).
3) Apply route-level RPS cap: 10rps per instance for 15m.
4) Ask Orbit to disable client-side auto-retries for 30–60m (already requested).

I’ve attached the CSV of request ids and the dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270620-0891.

— Monica
Support Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20 09:48 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Orbit Commerce — triage notes (logs + hypothesis)

Confirmed on my side; I can reproduce a KC miss storm in our staging harness within minutes using the orbit checkout workload. Quick notes:
- Root cause appears to be a race when a KV shard is under eviction: cache lookup returns transient miss and we spin up full compute; the fallback path incorrectly marks the request as eligible for "batch-coalesce-everyone" which bypasses some prioritization, producing oversized batches.
- Oversized batches drive CPU runaway on affected workers and queueing causes gateway 504s and upstream 429s as clients retry.

Immediate actions I will take now:
- Push a route-level config change to reduce coalescing window to 8–12ms and disable prefix caching for the orbit-checkout.v1 route (will rollout via canary to 10% first).
- Add a temporary per-route request cap and emergency circuit-breaker for queue length.
- Prepare a hotfix branch: kvcache-fallback-fix-20270620 (will open PR).

ETA for config roll (canary): ~12 minutes. If canary looks good, full roll in 10 more minutes.

— Markus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Thalia / Jake —
Thanks for rapidly sending the traces. Team has a targeted mitigation plan we’ll apply right now:
- Canaries rolling: reduce batch coalescing window and disable prefix cache on orbit-checkout.v1 (10% -> 100% if stable).
- Temporary per-route RPS cap and emergency circuit-breaker to prevent queue runaway.
- We ask Orbit to hold retries and non-essential writes for 30–60m while we stabilize.

We’re on the bridge now: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210. Monica will monitor the dashboard and Markus will push the canary. If you’d like, we can also route 5% of traffic to a model-variant with no prefix cache for further isolation.

As a goodwill gesture for the impact to your launch window, we’ll apply a service credit — will follow up with details.

— Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

We’ll need an RCA and timeline for the permanent fix to the kvcache fallback path — our compliance team wants to understand mitigations before we resume full launch. Can you share the incident timeline and planned fix ETA?

Thalia
